passages.text: Then Job answered: “Yes, I know that it is so, but how can a mortal be righteous before God?
passages.sermon:
Job spoke.
Job answered his friends.
Job said, “I know this is true.
God is holy and just.
People are only human.
How can any person be righteous before God?”
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ אָ֭מְנָם יָדַ֣עְתִּי כִי־ כֵ֑ן וּמַה־ יִּצְדַּ֖ק אֱנ֣וֹשׁ עִם־ אֵֽל׃

passages.text: If one wished to contend with God, he could not answer Him one time out of a thousand.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about God.
God is all-powerful.
God is perfectly wise.
A person may want to argue with God.
A person cannot answer God.
A person cannot answer even one question out of a thousand from God.
passages.original: אִם־ יַ֭חְפֹּץ לָרִ֣יב עִמּ֑וֹ לֹֽא־ יַ֝עֲנֶ֗נּוּ אַחַ֥ת מִנִּי־ אָֽלֶף׃

passages.text: God is wise in heart and mighty in strength. Who has resisted Him and prospered?
passages.sermon: God is wise in heart.\r\nGod is mighty in strength.\r\nNo one has resisted God and prospered.
passages.original: חֲכַ֣ם לֵ֭בָב וְאַמִּ֣יץ כֹּ֑חַ מִֽי־ הִקְשָׁ֥ה אֵ֝לָ֗יו וַיִּשְׁלָֽם׃

passages.text: He moves mountains without their knowledge and overturns them in His anger.
passages.sermon:
God is powerful.
God moves mountains.
The mountains do not know when God moves them.
God overturns mountains when He is angry.
passages.original: הַמַּעְתִּ֣יק הָ֭רִים וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֑עוּ אֲשֶׁ֖ר הֲפָכָ֣ם בְּאַפּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He shakes the earth from its place, so that its foundations tremble.
passages.sermon:
God is wise in heart.
God is mighty in strength.
God shakes the earth from its place.
The earth’s foundations tremble.
passages.original: הַמַּרְגִּ֣יז אֶ֭רֶץ מִמְּקוֹמָ֑הּ וְ֝עַמּוּדֶ֗יהָ יִתְפַלָּצֽוּן׃

passages.text: He commands the sun not to shine; He seals off the stars.
passages.sermon:
God has great power.
God commands the sun.
The sun does not shine when God commands it.
God seals the stars.
The stars do not give their light when God seals them.
passages.original: הָאֹמֵ֣ר לַ֭חֶרֶס וְלֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ח וּבְעַ֖ד כּוֹכָבִ֣ים יַחְתֹּֽם׃

passages.text: He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.
passages.sermon: God acts alone.\r\nGod stretches out the heavens by Himself.\r\nGod walks on the waves of the sea.
passages.original: נֹטֶ֣ה שָׁמַ֣יִם לְבַדּ֑וֹ וְ֝דוֹרֵ֗ךְ עַל־ בָּ֥מֳתֵי יָֽם׃

passages.text: He is the Maker of the Bear and Orion, of the Pleiades and the constellations of the south.
passages.sermon:
God is the Maker.
He made the Bear constellation.
He made the Orion constellation.
He made the Pleiades constellation.
He made the constellations in the southern sky.
passages.original: עֹֽשֶׂה־ עָ֭שׁ כְּסִ֥יל וְכִימָ֗ה וְחַדְרֵ֥י תֵמָֽן׃

passages.text: He does great things beyond searching out, and wonders without number.
passages.sermon:
God does great things.
No one can fully understand them.
God does wonders.
No one can count them.
passages.original: עֹשֶׂ֣ה גְ֭דֹלוֹת עַד־ אֵ֣ין חֵ֑קֶר וְנִפְלָא֗וֹת עַד־ אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃

passages.text: Were He to pass by me, I would not see Him; were He to move, I would not recognize Him.
passages.sermon:
God is the Maker of the stars and the constellations.
God does great things that no one can fully understand.
God performs wonders that no one can count.
If God passes by me, I do not see Him.
If God moves near me, I do not recognize Him.
passages.original: הֵ֤ן יַעֲבֹ֣ר עָ֭לַי וְלֹ֣א אֶרְאֶ֑ה וְ֝יַחֲלֹ֗ף וְֽלֹא־ אָבִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If He takes away, who can stop Him? Who dares to ask Him, ‘What are You doing?’
passages.sermon:
God has unlimited power.
No one can stop God if He takes something away.
No one can challenge God’s actions.
No one can ask God, “What are You doing?”
passages.original: הֵ֣ן יַ֭חְתֹּף מִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ מִֽי־ יֹאמַ֥ר אֵ֝לָ֗יו מַֽה־ תַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: God does not restrain His anger; the helpers of Rahab cower beneath Him.
passages.sermon:
God does not hold back His anger.
The helpers of Rahab bow down under Him.
They cower before His power.
No one can stand against God’s anger.
God is mighty and feared.
Rahab’s helpers are powerless before Him.
passages.original: אֱ֭לוֹהַּ לֹא־ יָשִׁ֣יב אַפּ֑וֹ תַּחַתוֹ שָׁ֝חֲח֗וּ עֹ֣זְרֵי רָֽהַב׃

passages.text: How then can I answer Him or choose my arguments against Him?
passages.sermon:
God is all-powerful.
God cannot be challenged.
I cannot answer God.
I cannot choose arguments against God.
passages.original: אַ֭ף כִּֽי־ אָנֹכִ֣י אֶֽעֱנֶ֑נּוּ אֶבְחֲרָ֖ה דְבָרַ֣י עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For even if I were right, I could not answer. I could only beg my Judge for mercy.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about God.
God is the Judge.
Job says, "Even if I am right, I cannot answer God."
I can only beg my Judge for mercy.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִם־ צָ֭דַקְתִּי לֹ֣א אֶעֱנֶ֑ה לִ֝מְשֹׁפְטִ֗י אֶתְחַנָּֽן׃

passages.text: If I summoned Him and He answered me, I do not believe He would listen to my voice.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about God.
Job feels small before God.
Job says, “If I call to God, and He answers me, I still do not believe He listens to my voice.”
Job doubts that God truly hears him.
Job feels distant from God, even if God seems to respond.
passages.original: אִם־ קָרָ֥אתִי וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֑נִי לֹֽא־ אַ֝אֲמִ֗ין כִּֽי־ יַאֲזִ֥ין קוֹלִֽי׃

passages.text: For He would crush me with a tempest and multiply my wounds without cause.
passages.sermon:
God is powerful.
God can act with overwhelming force.
God could crush me like a storm.
God could give me many wounds.
God could do this even if I have done nothing wrong.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁר־ בִּשְׂעָרָ֥ה יְשׁוּפֵ֑נִי וְהִרְבָּ֖ה פְצָעַ֣י חִנָּֽם׃

passages.text: He does not let me catch my breath, but overwhelms me with bitterness.
passages.sermon:
God acts with great power.
God does not let me rest.
God does not let me catch my breath.
God fills me with bitterness.
God overwhelms me with sorrow.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יִ֭תְּנֵנִי הָשֵׁ֣ב רוּחִ֑י כִּ֥י יַ֝שְׂבִּעַ֗נִי מַמְּרֹרִֽים׃

passages.text: If it is a matter of strength, He is indeed mighty! If it is a matter of justice, who can summon Him ?
passages.sermon:
God is strong.
God is mighty.
If strength is needed, God has all power.
If justice is needed, no one can call God to account.
No one can summon God to court.
No one can judge God.
passages.original: אִם־ לְכֹ֣חַ אַמִּ֣יץ הִנֵּ֑ה וְאִם־ לְ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט מִ֣י יוֹעִידֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Even if I were righteous, my mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would declare me guilty.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
Job says, “Even if I am righteous, my own mouth would condemn me.”
He says, “If I am blameless, my mouth would still declare me guilty.”
passages.original: אִם־ אֶ֭צְדָּק פִּ֣י יַרְשִׁיעֵ֑נִי תָּֽם־ אָ֝֗נִי וַֽיַּעְקְשֵֽׁנִי׃

passages.text: Though I am blameless, I have no concern for myself; I despise my own life.
passages.sermon:
I am blameless.
I do not understand myself.
I have no concern for my own life.
I despise my life.
passages.original: תָּֽם־ אָ֭נִי לֹֽא־ אֵדַ֥ע נַפְשִׁ֗י אֶמְאַ֥ס חַיָּֽי׃

passages.text: It is all the same, and so I say, ‘He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.’
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about God.
Job says everything is the same for everyone.
God destroys the blameless.
God destroys the wicked.
God treats both the blameless and the wicked the same.
passages.original: אַחַ֗ת הִ֥יא עַל־ כֵּ֥ן אָמַ֑רְתִּי תָּ֥ם וְ֝רָשָׁ֗ע ה֣וּא מְכַלֶּֽה׃

passages.text: When the scourge brings sudden death, He mocks the despair of the innocent.
passages.sermon:
God holds power over life and death.
He can send a scourge that kills suddenly.
Innocent people may suffer and die without warning.
God sees the despair of the innocent.
He mocks their suffering.
passages.original: אִם־ שׁ֭וֹט יָמִ֣ית פִּתְאֹ֑ם לְמַסַּ֖ת נְקִיִּ֣ם יִלְעָֽג׃

passages.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He blindfolds its judges. If it is not He, then who is it?
passages.sermon:
God gives the earth to wicked people.
God covers the faces of its judges.
God makes the judges unable to see justice.
If God does not do this, no one else does it.
No one else has this power except God.
passages.original: אֶ֤רֶץ׀ נִתְּנָ֬ה בְֽיַד־ רָשָׁ֗ע פְּנֵֽי־ שֹׁפְטֶ֥יהָ יְכַסֶּ֑ה אִם־ לֹ֖א אֵפ֣וֹא מִי־ הֽוּא׃

passages.text: My days are swifter than a runner; they flee without seeing good.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about his life.
He says his days pass very quickly.
His days move faster than a runner.
His days hurry away.
His days do not see any good.
passages.original: וְיָמַ֣י קַ֭לּוּ מִנִּי־ רָ֑ץ בָּֽ֝רְח֗וּ לֹא־ רָא֥וּ טוֹבָֽה׃

passages.text: They sweep by like boats of papyrus, like an eagle swooping down on its prey.
passages.sermon: My days pass quickly.\r\nThey move as fast as boats made of papyrus.\r\nThey rush by like an eagle swooping down on its prey.
passages.original: חָ֭לְפוּ עִם־ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת אֵבֶ֑ה כְּ֝נֶ֗שֶׁר יָט֥וּשׂ עֲלֵי־ אֹֽכֶל׃

passages.text: If I were to say, ‘I will forget my complaint and change my expression and smile,’ I would still dread all my sufferings; I know that You will not acquit me.
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
He speaks about his pain.
He says, “If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint,’ I try to leave my sadness behind.
I try to change my face and smile.
But I am still afraid of all my suffering.
I know that You, God, will not declare me innocent.”
passages.original: אִם־ אָ֭מְרִי אֶשְׁכְּחָ֣ה שִׂיחִ֑י אֶעֶזְבָ֖ה פָנַ֣י וְאַבְלִֽיגָה׃ יָגֹ֥רְתִּי כָל־ עַצְּבֹתָ֑י יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּי־ לֹ֥א תְנַקֵּֽנִי׃

passages.text: Since I am already found guilty, why should I labor in vain?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
He says he is already found guilty.
He asks why he should work for nothing.
He sees no purpose in his efforts.
He feels his labor is in vain.
passages.original: אָנֹכִ֥י אֶרְשָׁ֑ע לָמָּה־ זֶּ֝֗ה הֶ֣בֶל אִיגָֽע׃

passages.text: If I should wash myself with snow and cleanse my hands with lye, then You would plunge me into the pit, and even my own clothes would despise me.
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
Job believes God will not acquit him.
Job says, "If I wash myself with snow,"
"If I cleanse my hands with lye,"
"You, God, would still plunge me into the pit."
"Even my own clothes would despise me."
passages.original: אִם־ הִתְרָחַ֥צְתִּי בְמוֹ שָׁ֑לֶג וַ֝הֲזִכּ֗וֹתִי בְּבֹ֣ר כַּפָּֽי׃ אָ֭ז בַּשַּׁ֣חַת תִּטְבְּלֵ֑נִי וְ֝תִֽעֲב֗וּנִי שַׂלְמוֹתָֽי׃

passages.text: For He is not a man like me, that I can answer Him, that we can take each other to court.
passages.sermon:
God is not a man like me.
I cannot answer Him as I would answer a man.
We cannot go together to court as equals.
God is different from me.
I cannot challenge Him in judgment.
passages.original: כִּי־ לֹא־ אִ֣ישׁ כָּמֹ֣נִי אֶֽעֱנֶ֑נּוּ נָב֥וֹא יַ֝חְדָּ֗ו בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: Nor is there a mediator between us, to lay his hand upon us both.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job says there is no mediator between them.
No one stands between Job and God.
No one can place his hand on both Job and God.
No one can bring them together.
passages.original: לֹ֣א יֵשׁ־ בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ מוֹכִ֑יחַ יָשֵׁ֖ת יָד֣וֹ עַל־ שְׁנֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Let Him remove His rod from me, so that His terror will no longer frighten me.
passages.sermon:
God is not a man like me.
God is powerful and holy.
God judges me.
God uses His rod to discipline me.
I ask God to take His rod away from me.
I do not want God to punish me.
I do not want to be afraid of God's terror.
I want God to stop frightening me.
passages.original: יָסֵ֣ר מֵעָלַ֣י שִׁבְט֑וֹ וְ֝אֵמָת֗וֹ אַֽל־ תְּבַעֲתַֽנִּי׃

passages.text: Then I would speak without fear of Him. But as it is, I am on my own.
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
\r\nJob feels alone.
\r\nJob says, “If I had a mediator, I would speak.”
\r\nI would not be afraid of God.
\r\nBut I do not have a mediator.
\r\nI am alone before God.
passages.original: אַֽ֭דַבְּרָה וְלֹ֣א אִירָאֶ֑נּוּ כִּ֥י לֹא־ כֵ֥ן אָ֝נֹכִ֗י עִמָּדִֽי׃
